blockers.summary: Release blocked by SRU team (block-proposed-noble)

autopkgtest failure/regression reported: "…e StableReleaseUpdates policy regarding autopkgtest regressions [1]. https://ubuntu-archive-team.ubuntu.com/proposed-migration/noble/updat…" (ubuntu-sru-bot)
Regression mentioned: "…Potential regression: libvirt RBD storage pools on noble Upstream Ceph 19.2.6 removed the deprecate…" (mstevens-imt-systems)
Regression mentioned: "…d-party software involved. So this is a regression for any noble host using libvirt RBD storage pools, not just CloudStack. Note…" (mstevens-imt-systems)

Ceph 19.2.6 in noble-proposed removed the `auth_supported` option, so libvirt RBD storage pools fail to start ("failed to set RADOS option: auth_supported"). The regression was reproduced with archive-only packages. Noble libvirt 10.0.0-2ubuntu8.19 has no fix, and the ceph package has no compatibility patch. Either the libvirt fix (upstream commit 3af8cc5, tested patch attached) or a ceph patch restoring the option must be released before or with 19.2.6.

The block-proposed-noble tag is still set. Ceph 20.2.4 must reach resolute and stonking first, because everything in 19.2.6 (the CVE fix and CephX key handling) has to be in the newer series. Otherwise upgrades from 19.2.6 to an unpatched 20.x would hit authentication failures. The 20.2.4 upload was still sitting in resolute unapproved as of the last update.

Unresolved kernel-related decisions about the CVE change and its effect on other projects, plus how the change is communicated, are holding back the release. The verification-done tag was removed for this reason, and the status is unclear.
The libvirt/arm64 autopkgtest regression was reported against ceph 19.2.6 in noble-proposed. No comment shows it being investigated or cleared, and it may be related to the `auth_supported` breakage.
The caracal UCA verification is still marked needed (verification-caracal-needed). The Caracal package also carries the `auth_supported` removal, which affects libvirt there too.

comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…to 64. This could produce a performance regression for some users, as the performance bottleneck of this cap was significant enoug…" (whershberger)

The backported patches parse /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, so the default value is always used and the system limit is never honoured. The upstream fix is not yet merged, and the SRU would ship known-broken code unless the correction is included.

The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX, which makes the hard cap ineffective. The conservative fix (65530) is only submitted upstream, not merged, and must be included in the SRU.

The fix reads /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count, so libvirt's AppArmor profile must allow it. The libvirt change (LP #2170732) is still pending, and qemu would need a versioned Breaks on libvirt to force the upgrade. Without both, the new code may be denied access to the file or misbehave under confinement.

The fix only reduces the likelihood of hitting the limit and does not eliminate it. A QEMU guest still crashes with 'failed to set up stack guard page' at the noble limit (1048576) with 255 vCPUs. The Impact section and the test plan must state this residual risk clearly.

The analysis is incomplete. Live-migration threads' contribution to cached coroutines is unexplored. The reproducer and the Impact text have changed repeatedly, so regression and verification coverage may be insufficient.
